doc.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Cincinnati bands, race and the road to college
title: Why Wilberforce and not Oberlin or the Cincinnati Conservatory
summary: His mother wanted Oberlin or the Cincinnati Conservatory, which excluded blacks, but he applied too late and went to Wilberforce.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I want to come back to that, because I think there’s more in that and the perceptions that were going on about the period in music, but let’s go back to the transition from Cincinnati to Wilberforce.
Did you go there because your mother was there? You said at one point she ­ -

There were a couple of reasons. My mother had gone there. Also I had waited too late to apply for admission at Oberlin. My mother really wanted me to go to Oberlin Conservatory. I have to mention certain other factors here. She really wanted me to go to the Cincinnati Conservatory, which at the time was not admitting blacks. This is 1946, okay?
